open_questions.q: Does the graph-coupling classification stay stable when the free-energy invariants are extracted from real DFT-derived coupling coefficients rather than symmetry-only edges?
open_questions.basis: We used symmetry-allowed edges without DFT coupling magnitudes; the eta mixing ratios came from the paper's reported coefficients.
open_questions.next_steps: Compute trilinear/biquadratic coefficients via DFT frozen-phonon fits for LaGaO3/SrTiO3 superlattices and re-derive eta.

open_questions.q: Is the mixing metric eta = min/max of the two coupling channels the paper's exact definition, or an approximation that happens to match at ~21% and ~56%?
open_questions.basis: eta reproduced the paper values to <1% but the paper's precise metric definition was reconstructed from context.
open_questions.next_steps: Locate the paper's explicit eta definition and confirm the two matched cases are not coincidental.

open_questions.q: How does the classification behave for materials with THREE or more competing primary modes (beyond the (q2,q3) improper pair)?
open_questions.basis: All worked examples reduced to a polar mode induced by one dominant coupling path.
open_questions.next_steps: Apply the graph framework to a multi-order-parameter system (e.g. a hybrid improper ferroelectric with rotation+tilt+polar) and check for triggered vs mixed verdicts.

open_questions.q: Does the HfO2 Pca2_1 'no proper component' result survive when the parent is taken as the tetragonal P4_2/nmc phase rather than cubic Fm-3m?
open_questions.basis: We used Fm-3m as parent; HfO2's polar phase is often referenced to a tetragonal parent.
open_questions.next_steps: Redo the irrep compatibility with P4_2/nmc as parent and compare the proper-component verdict.

open_questions.q: Can the graph representation predict switching-barrier or coercive-field trends, or is it purely a static character classifier?
open_questions.basis: The method classifies distortion character but was not connected to dynamics.
open_questions.next_steps: Correlate graph coupling-path length/strength with computed NEB switching barriers across the example set.
